problem_disposition.summary: A structured prior-art hunt is needed before custom code gets built: re-problem, blind-parallel multi-source sweep with snowballing, hands-on probing, context-weighted judging, an imperative gate, and a durable record/learn loop. No single found candidate covers the whole loop.

candidate_comparisons.summary: The near-match: an 8-stage pipeline (DETECT→…→VERDICT→RECORD), a working stdlib-only scout script hitting GitHub+npm+crates+OpenSSF Scorecard, a 4-verdict model, SPDX license buckets, an ADR template. Verified hands-on: the script runs clean, no keys required. Covers Trigger strongly and Judge/Record partially; misses Re-problem, Snowball, Probe, and Learn entirely, and the Gate is explicitly advisory rather than imperative.

candidate_comparisons.summary: "Search GitHub before answering" — no verdict, no scoring. Thin coverage of Trigger and Sweep only; every other stage is unaddressed.

Mature, 31k+-star index for finding installable agent skills — solves a different problem (skill discovery, not prior-art verdicts). Not a competitor for the full loop; wired in separately as a Sweep lane (see the companion depend-skill-reuse exemplar).
Broader than code (tools, protocols, governance) with confidence-tagged findings, but welded into its own host runtime and not extractable as a standalone loop.
"Stop Your AI Agent From Building Tools That Already Exist" — a scan→score→recommend essay with a reuse/adapt/build verdict. Concept only, no implementation to adopt.

uncertainty.residual: five of nine stages (Re-problem, Snowball, Probe, Gate-as-imperative, Learn) had no found prior art to compare against at all, per the design.md §6 comparison table; the sweep that produced this table was not exhaustive, so a fuller-coverage skill that wasn't surfaced by the vocabularies tried cannot be ruled out.
uncertainty.confidence: high — the comparison table cites four real candidates plus one essay, none of which covers more than a partial subset of the nine stages, and the gap was itself the basis on which a human approved the build

reversibility: low once shipped and adopted — a multi-stage skill with its own schema, scripts, and evals is not a one-line revert; this is exactly why the BUILD verdict required human gating rather than proceeding on agent authority alone

route_components.output_boundary: the full nine-stage deja-vu skill: SKILL.md router, references/*.md per-stage detail, scripts/sweep.py + provenance.py + doctor.py, schemas/decision-packet.schema.json, and the evals/tests suite

custom_delta.maintenance_surface: the entire nine-stage loop: trigger description, all reference docs, sweep/provenance/doctor scripts, decision-packet schema, and the trigger/verdict eval suite

accepted_obligations: record this hunt's own receipts in docs/design.md §6 so a later re-hunt on "is there already a prior-art skill" starts from citation, not from scratch
route_components.residual_uncertainty: stages 4 (Snowball), 5 (Probe), 7 (Gate as imperative), and 9 (Learn) had no prior art to build on at all; their designs are the least externally validated parts of the shipped skill
route_components.next_action: none — shipped; re-run this hunt if a new candidate closes the identified stage gaps
